entries.title: Child among three killed in Russian missile attacks near Kyiv
entries.snippet: Russia continued its overnight attacks after President Volodymyr Zelensky warned of Ukraine's dwindling supplies of missile interceptors.

entries.title: Trump's ex-lawyer Todd Blanche narrowly confirmed as US attorney general
entries.snippet: The vote cements Trump's former criminal defence lawyer as the nation's top law enforcement official despite a rare pushback from some Republicans.

entries.title: The phone book that led us to Assad's spy chief in hiding
entries.snippet: How we tracked down "The Spider" who was once one of the most-feared men in Syria.

entries.title: Spain imposes border controls against Italy as row over Ceuta migrant influx intensifies
entries.snippet: Italy introduced border controls following an influx of about 78,000 migrants from Morocco into the neighbouring Spanish exclave of Ceuta.

entries.title: US pledges $1bn support to Colombia as Trump-backed president sworn in
entries.snippet: Abelardo de la Espriella used his maiden speech to promise an "all-out war" on what he calls "narco-terrorism".

entries.title: NBA forward Clarke's death due to effects of drugs
entries.snippet: Memphis Grizzlies forward Brandon Clarke's death was due to the effects of heroin and cocaine, the Los Angeles medical authority reveals.

entries.title: Thai PM vows to introduce stricter gun laws after eight killed in shooting
entries.snippet: Eight people were killed when a 14-year-old opened fire at his home and school before shooting himself dead.

entries.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan sign defence pact
entries.snippet: Pakistan says an attack on any of the three will amount to an attack against all, amid conflict in the Middle East.

entries.title: Spanish police arrest 78 people in bust of 'one of largest' smuggling networks
entries.snippet: The group moved synthetic drugs from Spain to Algeria, then used the return journey to smuggle migrants and weapons.

entries.title: Hunter Biden tells BBC his pardon was 'not good' for US or his father's legacy
entries.snippet: In a wide-ranging BBC interview, the former president's son denies any interest in running for office and says his father's cancer has spread.

entries.title: Book hidden in fireplace returned to Australian library 150 years overdue
entries.snippet: It is thought an apprentice stonemason who worked on the Houses of Parliament in London borrowed it.

entries.title: Kidnapped rare Serbian eagle freed into wild after rescue
entries.snippet: Feliks the eagle was abducted as he first flew the nest in Serbia and wound up in the Middle East with poachers who demanded a ransom.

entries.title: Sophia Laforteza steps away from Katseye, the second member to depart this year
entries.snippet: The announcement came comes after fellow bandmate Manon Bannerman went on a hiatus from the ensemble.

entries.title: Mexico and Peru restore diplomatic relations after asylum row
entries.snippet: Relations broke down after former Peruvian Prime Minister Betssy Chávez sought asylum in the Mexican embassy in November 2025.

entries.title: A new youth agitation grips an Indian state after 'cockroach' protests
entries.snippet: Weeks after the CJP protests shook Delhi, a new youth-led movement over jobs and recruitment is gathering force in Jharkhand.

entries.title: Meta fined $567m in largest child safety ruling against social media giant
entries.snippet: The ruling is in addition to $375m in fines Meta was already ordered to pay in the case, for a total of $942m.

entries.title: Trump administration to pay German firm $1.2bn to halt US wind projects
entries.snippet: The RWE payout is the latest in a string of deals cancelling wind energy projects, a power source long derided by Trump.

entries.title: Trump again tries to limit US birthright citizenship with new executive orders
entries.snippet: The executive orders ban birth tourism and expand the existing definition of people whose children are not eligible for US birthright citizenship.

entries.title: Australian aviation crew carries out daring midwinter Antarctica rescue
entries.snippet: Team evacuated a patient from McMurdo Station after landing plane in total darkness and temperature of -43°C.

entries.title: Trump denies US weapons shortage and says information 'leakers' being 'hunted down'
entries.snippet: While precise data is classified, publicly available information suggests the US has used up many difficult-to-manufacture weapons.

entries.title: Opinion: Europe's summer of heat
entries.snippet: Europe is in another brutal heat wave. The summer's earlier record-breaking weather already damaged crops, sparked wildfires and led to increased deaths.

entries.title: Switzerland is a neutral nation but has more nuclear bunkers than any country in the world
entries.snippet: Instead of scrapping its network of bomb shelters after the Cold War, Switzerland kept building them. The country has more than 370,000 nuclear bomb shelters. Some are now used to house migrants.

entries.title: The Women's Professional Baseball League makes its historic debut
entries.snippet: The Los Angeles Queens, the New York Heights, the Boston Hunters and the San Francisco Firebells take the field in Springfield, Ill., as the Women's Pro Baseball League kicks off its inaugural season.

entries.title: Federal funds can't be used to give test strips to drug users, raising overdose fears
entries.snippet: Drug addiction groups are reeling after Trump officials said federal grants cannot be used to hand out test strips to drug users. The strips help users check street drugs for dangerous adulterants.

entries.title: Private prisons announce $1.4 billion in revenue as immigration detentions climb
entries.snippet: That revenue does not include net proceeds of $1.6 billion made by CoreCivic after the recent sale of four of their facilities to the Department of Homeland Security.

entries.title: Data centers are a political issue crossing party lines, driving voters to candidates
entries.snippet: Wisconsin Democratic candidate for governor Francesca Hong called for a moratorium on data centers. So did Ohio Republican governor hopeful Vivek Ramaswamy, as data centers begin to dominate campaigns.

entries.title: Senate votes to confirm Todd Blanche as attorney general
entries.snippet: The Senate confirmed Blanche by a 50-49 vote early Saturday morning, elevating President Trump's former personal lawyer to head the Justice Department.

entries.title: Women in Maine may choose the victor in this year's Senate race
entries.snippet: The race between Susan Collins and Troy Jackson is one of the nation's most high-profile Senate contests this year -- and may ultimately be decided by an especially powerful voting bloc: Maine women.

entries.title: Trump renews push to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook
entries.snippet: Trump is once again threatening to fire Cook over unproven allegations of mortgage fraud after an earlier effort to remove Cook was struck down by the Supreme Court.

entries.title: Another court blocks White House ballroom work, teeing up a Supreme Court review
entries.snippet: A federal appeals court says above-ground construction cannot continue without approval from Congress, siding with historic preservation advocates.

entries.title: Advocates for former U.S. Marine held for years in Russia say he is near death
entries.snippet: A former U.S. Marine held in Russia for more than four years on disputed charges is gravely ill and at risk of dying, his family and advocates said Friday.

entries.title: ICE will only release body camera video when in agency's 'best interests,' policy says
entries.snippet: Immigration and Customs Enforcement is moving to equip officers with body cameras in the next two months but the agency's policy gives it broad control over what footage will be made public by specifying any releases must be in its "best interests."

entries.title: What the July jobs report reveals about the strength of the economy
entries.snippet: New labor data shows the U.S. economy lost 23,000 jobs in July, when economists had predicted modest growth. Revised numbers for May and June also show 103,000 fewer jobs created than originally reported. The unemployment rate ticked down, from 4.2% to 4.1%, a function of fewer p

entries.snippet: At the U.S. Capitol, it was a wild day of decision and indecision. The Senate passed the toughest sanctions bill on Russia yet and is also now on track to confirm Todd Blanche as attorney general. But a slew of other high-priority items are still tangled, largely due to a Republi

entries.title: Judge orders Virginia county to replace Confederate names it restored to schools in 2024
entries.snippet: A federal judge has sided with the Virginia NAACP in its lawsuit against a county school board's reinstatement of Confederate military names to two schools, saying the decision discriminated against Black students and ordering the board to change the schools' monikers again.

entries.title: What's holding up the Iran-Oman proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
entries.snippet: There is a new partnership in the Middle East and South Asia. Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed an agreement similar to NATO's Article 5, pledging that a strike against one of them would be considered a strike against all of them. But despite reports that it was close, no

entries.title: Colombia's new president reflects Latin America's right-wing shift
entries.snippet: The new president of Colombia was inaugurated on Friday. Abelardo de la Espriella won a tight race in June, ending Colombia's leftist movement with a sharp pivot to the right. Liz Landers takes a look at the president and his tight relationship with the Trump White House.

entries.title: Drought and aging infrastructure plunge Puerto Rico into a water crisis
entries.snippet: Puerto Rico is facing yet another crisis as major cities are rationing water for residents due to severe drought conditions. This problem is also exposing the island's aging water infrastructure and lack of immediate government action, leaving many frustrated. For more on how fam

entries.title: How Lahaina is recovering 3 years after the devastating fires
entries.snippet: It has been three years since the deadliest wildfires to hit the U.S. in more than a century swept through Lahaina on the island of Maui. The fires consumed thousands of structures, killed 102 people and destroyed an important site of Hawaiian history. Hundreds of homes have been

entries.title: Brooks and Capehart on what progressive primary wins mean for Democrats

entries.title: Helicopter battling Utah wildfire crashes with no word on the 2 people aboard
entries.snippet: The helicopter was one of seven working the fire in central Utah that was caused by lightning on July 27.

entries.title: Police release video showing gunman shooting victims at Idaho In-N-Out Burger drive-thru
entries.snippet: The video revealed more details of the chaotic scene last weekend. The gunman walked up to the drive-thru window four times and opened fire, killing an In-N-Out employee, police said.

entries.title: WATCH LIVE: Senate passes Graham's Russia sanctions bill, confirms dozens of nominees
entries.snippet: The Senate passed a sweeping Russia sanctions bill negotiated by the late Sen. Lindsey Graham on Friday.

entries.title: Live Results: Hawaii midterm primaries
entries.snippet: An ongoing corruption scandal involving Hawaii's lieutenant governor looms over Saturday's state primary as nine candidates jockey to replace her.

entries.title: Senate confirms Cameron Hamilton to lead FEMA and clears 73 other Trump nominees
entries.snippet: Hamilton was among a group of 74 nominations approved by the Senate, including President Donald Trump's pick to lead the Transportation Security Administration, David Cummins, and his choice for ambassador to Brazil, Daniel Perez.

entries.title: Trump administration proceeds with efforts to fire Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook
entries.snippet: The Trump administration is moving ahead with its efforts to fire Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook, two months after the Supreme Court allowed her to retain her job while she fights the president's effort to terminate her over mortgage fraud allegations that she has denied.

entries.title: Lindsay Clancy trial spotlights psychiatric hospital stay before she killed her 3 children
entries.snippet: Clancy's stay is a key chapter in both the prosecution and defense narratives about her mental state when she strangled the children in their suburban home and then jumped out a second-story window.

entries.title: Appeals court rules Trump can't build White House ballroom without congressional approval
entries.snippet: Trump said in a post on social media that he would be appealing what he called an "unjust decision" to the U.S. Supreme Court.

entries.title: Senate passes sweeping Russia sanctions bill negotiated by the late Sen. Lindsey Graham
entries.snippet: The bipartisan legislation, which passed the Senate 86-11, would penalize countries that continue to buy Russian oil, gas and other exports seeking to deprive Putin of revenues fueling the war.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: EU holds talks with big tech over Ceuta misinformation
entries.snippet: EU digital chief Henna Virkkunen has called for closer monitoring of social media platforms moving forward, amid the spread of misinformation during the recent migrant influx at Spain's Ceuta.

entries.title: When German Catholics and Protestants share a church
entries.snippet: Each year, dozens of churches are decommissioned, demolished or repurposed in Germany. But there is a new, unique development.

entries.title: Germany news: Trucking rules eased as rivers run low
entries.snippet: Several states will let trucks use motorways on Sundays and holidays as freight shipping is hampered by low water levels. The body of a German sailor missing for days has been found in the southern Aegean. DW has more.

entries.title: India wary of potential 100% US tariffs over Russian oil
entries.snippet: The US Senate passed a sanctions bill that could result in tariffs on India as a major consumer of Russian oil. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: Typhoon Dolphin hits Japan as China braces for coming storm
entries.snippet: A typhoon is lashing Japan's south, causing injuries and blackouts. It is now headed for China, where ports have been closed in preparation.

entries.title: Germany debates reintroducing mandatory civilian service
entries.snippet: Social organizations are skeptical about the government's ideas for a civilian service program that youths could choose as an alternative should Germany reinstate mandatory military conscription.

entries.title: Ceuta: Spain sets up border controls on travelers from Italy
entries.snippet: Spain had warned Italy it would impose entry checks on visitors unless Rome halts its controls by Sunday. Even though they don't share a land border, the countries entered a spat after the Ceuta border rush.

entries.title: Colombia: Trump ally De la Espriella takes office
entries.snippet: Conservative Abelardo de la Espriella was sworn in as Colombia's president, promising to crack down on armed drug gangs.

entries.title: Iceland’s EU vote: A nation divided over Europe
entries.snippet: Security concerns, control over fishing rights and rising living costs are shaping Iceland's debate over whether to restart talks on joining the European Union.

entries.title: Migrant tunnels in Lithuania direct suspicion towards Minsk
entries.snippet: Lithuania's border guards have discovered tunnels through which migrants are trying to enter the country from Belarus. Analysts see them as a means to destabilize the country.

entries.title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy makes first visit to Russia-friendly Serbia
entries.snippet: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy is making his first visit to Serbia. His host, President Aleksandar Vucic, hopes to score points with the EU, while Zelenskyy seeks more arms from a country that remains friendly to Russia.

entries.title: Trump to appeal ballroom construction halt to Supreme Court
entries.snippet: A US Court of Appeals upheld a ruling that saying Trump cannot build a White House ballroom without congressional approval. The president vowed to appeal what he called an "unjust decision."

entries.title: How viable is the potential Iran-Oman Hormuz shipping deal?
entries.snippet: Iran says a shipping accord with Oman is in its final stages, but analysts warn sanctions, security concerns and rival US-Iran goals could limit its impact.

entries.title: Berlin clubs struggle as drink sales dry up and costs rise
entries.snippet: Berlin's clubs are still drawing crowds, but shorter nights, fewer alcohol sales and rising costs have changed their business model. Door fees, rather than bar takings, are increasingly their real financial lifeline.

entries.title: Eco wins: Hungary goes solar, marmots go viral and Rome gets an upgrade
entries.snippet: From Hungary's accidental solar revolution to marmot crowdfunding and a long-overdue upgrade for Rome's big snake, good news comes in strange packages this week.

entries.title: Thailand: Several killed in school shooting north of Bangkok
entries.snippet: The shooting incident took place at the Debsirin Nonthaburi School in ​the ‌Bang Kruai district of Nonthaburi, just north of the capital city of Bangkok. Several people were killed in the attack.

entries.title: Europe's rivers are drying up. Can they be saved?
entries.snippet: The Rhine and Danube have reached historic lows. Dwindling water levels are affecting shipping, agriculture and ecosystems — and raising concerns about the future of drinking water supplies.

entries.title: Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing seeks legitimacy in Thailand
entries.snippet: Bangkok rolled out the red carpet for the Myanmar leader, but experts say the former junta chief still faces major obstacles in his bid for regional acceptance.

entries.title: Germany: Far-right AfD extends its lead in nationwide polls
entries.snippet: In the latest Sunday poll, the AfD continues to pull ahead. And more and more people are against excluding the right-wing populists from decision-making, at least on a case-by-case basis.
